title: H. Holbeck to Rowland Browne, merchant's letter of 10 March 1550/51, three pages in cipher (Hatfield House, Cecil Papers CP 150/143)

documents.shelfmark: Hatfield House, Cecil Papers CP 150/143 (three pages; page 3 is f. 144); HMC Salisbury Part I (1883), p. 85, no. 349

plaintext.source: HMC, Calendar of the Cecil Papers, Part I (1883), p. 85, no. 349, summarises the cipher part (28 pipes of oil, proceedings against Rowland Browne by merchants of Edinburgh, other mercantile matters); no decipherment printed.

transcription.source: Free PDF copy supplied by the Hatfield House archives, 16 Nov 2026, for private study; images not reproduced and not to be republished
transcription.notes: Transcribed by shape (codes in NOTES.md). Pages 1-2: one blind pass by a sub-agent (pass 1 not made). Page 3: two independent passes (pass 1, and a blind pass 2 in frozen/transcription/), not yet reconciled on the image. Counts exclude sums in clear figures and [?]: 1,029 words, 4,332 signs, 26 shapes. Shape confusions 2/j/z, D/Q and the '10'-like sign are the main noise.

system.summary: Simple substitution of English with words separated by points; many letters keep their own secretary-hand shape (t, h, e, o, b), the rest are signs, several shaped like digits (4 = a, 8 = w, 9 = g, 7 = p, 2 = i/y/k). Sums are written in clear figures.
system.notes: 26 distinct shapes over 4,332 signs as transcribed; some shapes cover two letters in the frozen key (D = s/d, Q = l/d, z = r/k, 2 = i/y/k), which may be transcription confusion rather than polyphony.

prior_solution.where: HMC Salisbury Part I (1883), p. 85, no. 349: the editor summarises the cipher part, so he read at least its drift; no decipherment or key printed. Nothing on DECODE, Tomokiyo or Lasry (catalogue 1015 vetting, 29 Oct 2026); no PR or issue on this letter on origin/main, 16 Nov 2026.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout asked Hatfield House for copies and chose the target; the rules were set before the key work (page 3 held out, HOLDOUT-DEF.md frozen; key, measure, lexicon and threshold frozen in PREREG.md; one measure). Claude Opus 5.5 agents transcribed, built the key on pages 1-2, measured once and wrote up. No human has read the decode.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (transcription, key, measure, write-up)

solution.what: Free PDF copy of CP 150/143 supplied by the Hatfield House archives for private study; shelfmark given in their reply (issue #712).
HMC Salisbury Part I p. 85 no. 349 read in the archive.org text: summary of the cipher part, no decipherment; origin/main catalogue, leads, PRs and issues checked.
Held-out portion fixed before any key work: the whole of page 3 (HOLDOUT-DEF.md, SHA-256 456e52f5...).
Transcribed by shape: pages 1-2 in one blind pass, page 3 in two independent passes (not reconciled on the image).

Key built on pages 1-2 only: simple substitution with many letters kept in their own shape; each sign given a small set of letters to absorb shape confusions; frozen (cle/key-FROZEN.json) with the measure and lexicon (PREREG.md).

One pre-registered measure on page 3 (pass 1): share of signs in words found in the lexicon after decoding, against 200 shuffled keys. 0.684, best null 0.501, mean 0.155; bar 0.85 and best null + 0.30. Secondary on pass 2: 0.676 (best null 0.450).

After the measure, not counted: the mechanical decode of page 3 is continuous English (ships stayed in Zealand, the exchange at 16s 8d usance, a ship for Berwick); the unrecognised words are names, 1551 spellings and shape confusions, so the lexicon and the transcription, not the key, look like the cause.

outcome.method_basis: Key built from the ciphertext of pages 1-2 (the HMC summary gave the subject, not a parallel text) and frozen; the one pre-registered measure on held-out page 3 failed (0.684 against 0.85 and best shuffled key + 0.30), so the key is partial and the text is not read.
outcome.fraction_read_source: transcription.txt: no reading file; the decode in decode_after_measure.txt is mechanical and not counted
